question: How many drugs are currently in shortage because of quality problems, and which of their manufacturing sites received an OAI classification in the last two fiscal years?
tier_reasons: verifier flagged unsupported or misattributed claims
2 interpretation(s) give materially different answers; shown side by side
part of the question cannot be answered from this data (disclosed)
headline: As of 2025-10-23, 6 drugs are in Current shortage for cGMP quality reasons, and 4 of their linked manufacturing sites had an OAI inspection in fiscal years 2024 and 2025.
markdown:
## Answer
As of 2025-10-23, 6 distinct drugs have a latest shortage status of Current with the reason "Quality: cGMP Issue" [E1]. Of their manufacturing sites, 4 received an OAI classification in fiscal years 2024 and 2025 [E1].

## Detail
- Drugs in scope: Ampicillin-Sulbactam, Cefepime HCl, Meropenem, Methotrexate Sodium, Piperacillin-Tazobactam and Vancomycin HCl [E1].
- Every one of the 6 shortage records was linked to a site, so 0 were left unlinked [E1].
- OAI site, Baxter Healthcare Corporation, FEI 3001234567, Deerfield, United States. Drug: Ampicillin-Sulbactam. Inspection ended 2025-07-06 (source inspections#L5) [E1].
- OAI site, Pfizer Manufacturing LLC, FEI 3002891456, McPherson, United States. Drug: Vancomycin HCl. Inspection ended 2024-03-25 (source inspections#L3) [E1].
- OAI site, ICU Medical Inc, FEI 3007445123, Lake Forest, United States. Drug: Piperacillin-Tazobactam. Inspection ended 2024-07-02 (source inspections#L2) [E1].
- OAI site, Fresenius Kabi USA LLC, FEI 3009123789, Wilson, United States. Drug: Cefepime HCl. Inspection ended 2025-07-10 (source inspections#L4) [E1].
- Each of these OAI inspections is in the project area Drug Quality Assurance and the product type Finished Dosage [E1].
- Linked sites with no OAI in the window: the Methotrexate Sodium site, Hospira Inc (FEI 3005678901), last inspected 2024-05-21. The Meropenem site (FEI 3007891234) has no inspection record [E1].

## Interpretation applied
- **Quality problems:** the reading used is strict, meaning "Quality: cGMP Issue" only. The alternate is broad, which adds Manufacturing Delay. Broad gives 15 distinct drugs across 21 records, against 6 under strict. Broad still gives the same 4 OAI sites [E1, E2].
- **Last two fiscal years:** the reading used is the completed fiscal years 2024 and 2025. The alternate includes the just-started current year, which gives fiscal years 2025 and 2026. That alternate leaves 2 OAI sites: Baxter Healthcare Corporation and Fresenius Kabi USA LLC. It drops Pfizer Manufacturing LLC and ICU Medical Inc, whose OAI inspections ended in fiscal year 2024 [E1, E3].
- **Fiscal year basis:** the reading used is inspection end date. The alternate is classification date. It gives the same 4 sites [E1, E4].
- **How many drugs:** distinct generic name, which here equals the record count of 6 [E1].
- **Currently:** the latest revision has status Current as of 2025-10-23 [E1].
- **Manufacturing site:** the facility operator reached through the application's manufacturing FEI. In the strict results the sponsor name matches the operator for every OAI site [E1].
- **OAI project area:** any project area counts, and each is shown per row [E1].

## Caveats
- Three strict-scope records have status Current but were last revised more than eighteen months before the as-of date. They are Cefepime HCl, Methotrexate Sodium and Piperacillin-Tazobactam. Their status is reported as recorded [E1].
- The Meropenem site, FEI 3007891234, has never been inspected. Its country is UNKNOWN, and none was inferred from the sponsor name [E1].
- Under broad scope, only 12 of 21 records link to a site. 9 reference applications missing from the applications file, including Morphine Sulfate, Doxorubicin HCl, Cisplatin and Furosemide [E2].
- Under broad scope, an Amoxicillin shortage has conflicting records, Resolved and then Current. The latest revision, Current, was used [E2].
- Under broad scope, some FEIs start with an unexpected digit, and the tool says to verify them before citing. None of the OAI sites above is affected [E1, E2].

## Cannot be answered from this data
- Whether any OAI finding caused or relates to a specific shortage. The data links shortage to application to facility, not to root cause [E1].
- Under broad scope, the manufacturing sites for the 9 unlinked records, because their applications are absent from the applications file [E2].
- The country and inspection history of FEI 3007891234 [E1].
- Whether the stale Current records are still truly current [E1].

gate.reason: Question is answerable from the Shortage, Application, Facility, and Inspection tables with stated defaults, but several ambiguous terms must be resolved and coverage disclosed. Count of current shortages due to quality problems can use reason_category='Quality: cGMP Issue' (strict scope) joined to shortage status Current; drug count at generic_name level by default (latest revision per shortage_id). Only 13 of 57 Current shortage rows resolve to an Application, so the quality/OAI linkage via related_application covers a small subset and must be disclosed. Manufacturing sites with OAI in the last two completed fiscal years (by inspection_end_date) can be listed via Application.manufacturing_fei → Facility → Inspection, with the caveat that the link from shortage to site is only available for resolved rows and that 'manufacturing site' is facility_operator by default.

output.reason: Question is answerable from the Shortage, Application, Facility, and Inspection tables with stated defaults, but several ambiguous terms must be resolved and coverage disclosed. Count of current shortages due to quality problems can use reason_category='Quality: cGMP Issue' (strict scope) joined to shortage status Current; drug count at generic_name level by default (latest revision per shortage_id). Only 13 of 57 Current shortage rows resolve to an Application, so the quality/OAI linkage via related_application covers a small subset and must be disclosed. Manufacturing sites with OAI in the last two completed fiscal years (by inspection_end_date) can be listed via Application.manufacturing_fei → Facility → Inspection, with the caveat that the link from shortage to site is only available for resolved rows and that 'manufacturing site' is facility_operator by default.

output.restated_question: Count distinct generic drugs with latest-revision shortage status Current whose reason_category is quality-related, and list their manufacturing sites (facility via application link) with an OAI inspection classification in the last two FDA fiscal years.

interpretations.default_reading: as of data max, status Current on latest revision

reasons: 2 ambiguous terms with materially different readings

divergent_interpretations.how: Broad scope (adds Manufacturing Delay) more than doubles the drug count, but the OAI site list is the same set of four facilities. Broad scope also brings in coverage loss: 9 of 21 records cannot be linked to a site, versus full linkage under strict.
Completed FY2024–FY2025 yields four OAI sites. Include-current (FY2025–FY2026, where FY2026 has only just begun) drops the two FY2024 OAIs (Pfizer McPherson, ICU Medical Lake Forest), leaving two.
Inspection end date and classification date put every OAI in the same fiscal year, so the results are identical.

cannot_answer: Whether the OAI finding caused or relates to the specific shortage: the data links shortage → application → facility, not root cause.

Under the broad scope, the manufacturing sites for 9 shortage records (e.g., Morphine, Doxorubicin, Cisplatin, Furosemide) cannot be determined because their applications are absent from applications.csv.
Country and inspection history for Meropenem's site FEI 3007891234: it has never been inspected, so country is UNKNOWN. Do not infer it from the sponsor name.
Whether the stale 'Current' records (Cefepime, Methotrexate, Piperacillin-Tazobactam, last revised >18 months ago) are still truly current.
output.analyst_notes: Lead with E1 (default: strict cGMP, completed FY2024–2025, inspection-end-date basis): count distinct generic drugs, name them, then name the four OAI facilities with FEI, city, inspection date, and row citation. All four are US sites and all OAIs are in Drug Quality Assurance / Finished Dosage. Note that every strict-scope record linked to a site (full coverage). Then present side by side: broad scope (E2) gives a larger drug count but the same four OAI sites, with coverage loss disclosed; include-current window (E3) cuts the list to two. State that FY basis made no difference (E4). Flag the three stale Current records and the never-inspected Meropenem site with UNKNOWN country. Use only FEIs returned by the tool. The strict-scope OAI FEIs all start with '3'; the '4'-prefix anomalies appear only in E2's non-OAI list and must not be cited without verification.
